title: Barrel Bath
text: After a while, a messenger from Siltvelt came to tell us that hot water had been secured. A partition was set up in one corner of the washing area, and my Father took a bath in a tub made of wood.
“How’s the water temperature? I can use Magic to warm it up if you’d like.”
“Yeah, it’s fine. Aren’t you going to get in, Motoyasu?”
“I’ll wait until you’re done, Father. Now, shall I wash your back?”
“U-uh, sure. It feels a bit strange to be called ‘Father’ and have my back washed by someone my own age, though…”

Ah, I miss Filo-tan. We once took a hot spring bath together on Cal Mira Island. Back then, I was still lusting after pigs and hadn’t yet awakened to my mission, but it’s a fond memory. If I had to say one thing, I really wish I’d saved some of Filo-tan’s leftover bathwater.

Besides, being cherished like this by my Father makes me feel truly happy. I scrub my Father’s back vigorously. Considering that this back carries the weight of the world, I must wash it thoroughly. Once I finished washing his back, my Father got back into the tub.
“Haa…”
My father let out a sigh, as if he were slightly tired.
“So that you can overcome any assassins who come, I plan to show you a way to become stronger starting now.”
“Yeah. I’ll do my best to become as strong as Motoyasu-kun, if possible.”
“Exactly. That way, you won’t have to run and hide—you’ll be able to turn the tables on assassins head-on!”
“I know, but… what’s the plan?”
“I told you before. Let’s put the plan into action starting tomorrow.”
My father didn’t seem to have a clue what I was talking about. I realized later that I’d actually mentioned that during the previous loop.
“That was a nice bath. Now then…”

Éclair began discussing something with the envoy from Siltvelt. The sun was just beginning to set. Apparently, when Éclair returned from her bath, there were reports of assassins lurking near the tavern. Since burly Demi-Human adventurers are staying at this tavern, they probably won’t confront us head-on, but it’s better to be safe than sorry.

In fact, a Demi-Human adventurer is standing guard right in front of the tavern. Since we’ve been staying here, my father is cooking in the kitchen. Both the tavern patrons and we are thoroughly enjoying the meal he’s served us.
“This is all I can do…”
My father says self-deprecatingly, but seeing him like this has really fired up the Demi-Human adventurers.
“It is our mission to protect the Shield Hero! Everyone, we’ll defend him at all costs!”
“Ooh!”

My father, looking slightly flustered by the outburst, is bustling about in the kitchen. He’s quite skilled, isn’t he? Just as I’d expect from my Father. In the first world, someone called him the “Hero of Food,” and he’s certainly living up to that name.
“My experience working part-time at an izakaya is coming in handy.”
“So you’ve done all sorts of things, haven’t you, Father?”
I seem to recall hearing secondhand that he used to work part-time at a food court. And I heard he was juggling multiple jobs at the same time, too.
“Well, yeah… Do you drink, Motoyasu-kun?”
“No, thanks. By the way, did you used to like drinking, Father?”

“Hmm… Actually, I’ve never gotten drunk, so I don’t really like it. People get completely sloshed and start rambling, and having to keep agreeing with the same story over and over again is exhausting, after all.”

Come to think of it, I heard you have a constitution that doesn’t get drunk. That brings back memories. Doubting the story that my father wouldn’t get drunk even after eating a Lucor Fruit, I once ate one myself and passed out. Just remembering how drunk I got back then is pure hell. Combined with the nightmare of being tended to by a pig, I’m starting to feel nauseous.
“Well then, I’ll whip up some snacks to go with the drinks, so everyone have a good time.”
I watched over him until my father finished cooking. Then, I headed over to where Éclair and the others were discussing things, accompanied by my Father.
“How did the meeting go?”
“Hmm… As for proposals, I’m leaning toward Lord Kitamura’s teleportation skill.”
“That sounds reasonable. Starting tomorrow, I intend to focus on training Filolial-sama. While I’m at it, I’ll go retrieve the portal.”
“Mr. Kitamura, I’m counting on you.”
“Understood.”
“Also, after discussing it with the people from Siltvelt, we plan to change our hideout to another building in town tomorrow by going through the sewers.”
“Through the sewers?”
“Yes, the arrangements for that are in place. After all, we need to completely shake off the assassins.”
Éclair glanced outside with an annoyed look. Then the sound of clashing swords reaches our ears.
“The Three Heroes Church… It’s only to be expected, of course, but it seems they don’t want Lord Iwatani to go to Siltvelt.”
“They’re using the commotion caused by the adventurers as a cover, but there’s no doubt about it.”

The commotion caused by what appeared to be drunken adventurers was quelled by the Demi-Humans in the tavern and the town’s vigilante group, but it certainly feels like it’s happening quite frequently. From downstairs, I’ve heard the phrase, “What kind of tavern is this? It reeks of Demi-Humans!” about three times so far. You’d think anyone would catch on after doing that so many times. I’d like to see a little more variety in how they pick fights, too. What’s more, I’ve heard that some members of the vigilante group may have been bribed—there were reports of people trying to get inside by picking strange fights.
Right now, the room we’re in is a secret room. Even outside of Melromarc, places like this must be common in neighboring countries.
“I intend to make my Father strong enough to fight back and defeat any assassins who attack him.”
“Ideally, I’d like to raise his level… but is that even possible?”
“Everything will be ready the day after tomorrow.”
“Understood. Then tomorrow, after Lord Kitamura departs, we’ll make our move. It might be dangerous, but we have no choice.”

In order to make my father-in-law and the others stronger, I, Motoyasu, must stay behind. It’s truly a nuisance. Once the problem is resolved, assassins won’t stand a chance against my father-in-law. I can say this because I’ve faced him as an enemy countless times and even fought alongside him as one of his subordinates. That night, for the first time in a long while, I was able to fall asleep while breathing in the scent of Filolial-sama’s egg.
The next day, before we set out.
“Oh, Motoyasu-kun. One of the eggs has a crack in it. I think it’s about to hatch, don’t you think?”

We’d been attacked four times during the night. It’s a dazzling morning after we finally defeated those scoundrels who even resorted to arson. I’m starting to feel like I just want to storm in through the portal and slaughter the Three Heroes Church and that bunch of Trash. But since Father and Éclair refuse, there’s nothing I can do about it.
When I turned my attention to the eggs, the very first one was just about to hatch. If I’m not mistaken, this is Filolial-sama—the one the farmer said was expensive.
“Peep!”
With a lively cry, Filolial-sama hatched. As for her color… she was a white Filolial-sama.
“Wow… she’s pure white.”
I placed Filolial-sama on my hand to take a closer look. Her gender… she’s a female. By the way, there are slightly more female Filolial-samas than males.
“What shall we name her?”

Actually, I’d been thinking of “Shiro-chan,” but since that’s a name I’d already given to a Filolial-sama before the loop, I’m debating whether to use it again. The Shiro-chan I knew was male, so this isn’t the same individual. Using that name would mean it’s a duplicate.
“Since it’s a Filolial-sama… ‘Filo’ would end up being the name of the girl Motoyasu-kun likes, wouldn’t it?”
“A white Filolial, huh…”
Éclair murmurs as she looks at the newly hatched chick.
“Did you also find romance in a prince riding a white horse, Éclair? Or rather, how would that be expressed in this world?”
“A hero riding a white bird… a hero riding a white griffin—oh, and there’s also the white flying dragon.”
“So the hero is a sure thing?”
“I suppose so… but even that dream…”
It feels like Éclair is thinking something rather rude. Is she about to say that my Father is unreliable or something?
“How rude! The sight of my Father riding Filolial-sama is truly majestic!”
“No, I was just thinking that after seeing Lord Kitamura!”
“Hahaha… Sorry, but I just couldn’t think of a comeback.”
Just as we were talking, the next egg cracked open.
“Peep!”
Next up… was a yellow Filolial-sama. They’re all so cute.
“Peep!”
Éclair placed it on her hand and handed it to me. As for its gender… it’s a male.
“Hmm, what should we name him?”
“Peep peep!”
“Would ‘Yellow’ be too obvious?”
“It’s a male, right? I thought about ‘Lemon’ because of the color, but it’d be a shame to call a boy ‘Lemon,’ wouldn’t it?”
While we were discussing names like that, the very last one hatched.
“Peep!”
And the one who finally kicked through the shell was a pink Filolial-sama. So close! If it had been white or cherry blossom pink, I would’ve tentatively given it the name “Filo-tan”…
